purpose: Random-unit-direction null for the rank-1 direction patch in BOTH patch directions (the committed direction_patch.csv has the null only for control_to_uncertain). Adds the missing baseline for the injection (uncertain_to_control) result.
script: scripts/circuit_direction_patch_u2c_null.py (copy of scripts/circuit_direction_patch.py; the only functional change is running each random direction in the uncertain_to_control direction too)

invocation.conflict: --category conflict --layers 11-21 --limit 60 --n-random 10 --seed 42 (164 working pairs fit the directions; 60 held-out pairs evaluated)

sanity_check: every row shared with the committed direction_patch.csv (direction both ways, random control_to_uncertain) reproduced bit-identically: max |diff| = 0.0 in log-odds and entropy recovery for both arms
stretch_control: direction_patch_u2c_hedgematched.csv: 10 random unit directions whose projections onto the 5 hedge-token unembedding rows (lm_head rows for ' not', ' I', ' unknown', ' unclear', ' no') are set equal to the real direction's (QR basis; max |W r - W d| = 3e-8; cos(r, d_real) ~ 1e-4), orthogonal remainder rescaled to unit norm. Conflict arm, uncertain_to_control: log-odds recovery -0.005 +- 0.023 (max +0.041), entropy +0.005, vs the real direction's +0.970 reproduced in the same run. Caveat: the real direction holds only 0.26% of its squared norm inside the hedge-unembedding span, so this null is only slightly stronger than the plain random one.
verdict: Injecting a random unit direction does not switch the hedge on (~30x below the real direction); the rank-1 injection result is direction-specific and survives matching the hedge-logit projection.
environment: molab sandbox, NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000, torch 2.11.0+cu130, transformers 5.14.1
